title: The Bar That Stretched 0.80 mm, Not 0.40
featured_title: THE BAR THAT STRETCHED 0.80 MM NOT 0.40
subject: civil

presentation.challenge: The stress was correct, but only half the member length was used in the deformation equation. The full bar stretched 0.80 mm.

practice.primary_question: How is elastic axial deformation of a prismatic bar calculated from load, length, area, and elastic modulus?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using the correct stress but the wrong member length in δ=PL/(AE).

case_dna.target_misconception: Axial elongation can be computed using only the loaded half of a uniformly stressed prismatic member.
case_dna.why_plausible: The load is applied at the end, and a diagram can make the load path look localized, but the entire member carries the same axial force.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For P=80 kN, L=2.0 m, A=1000 mm², and E=200 GPa, δ=PL/(AE)=0.80 mm.
case_dna.corrected_model: For a uniform prismatic bar under constant axial force, use the full loaded length in δ=PL/(AE).

problem_statement: A steel tie bar carries a constant axial tensile load P=80 kN. It is 2.0 m long, has cross-sectional area A=1000 mm², and elastic modulus E=200 GPa. Determine axial stress, strain, and elongation. A note uses only 1.0 m of length and reports 0.40 mm.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The correct stress was applied over only half the bar.
gates.prompt: What member length experiences the axial strain?

options.label: δ=PL/(AE)
options.reason: A uniform prismatic bar under constant axial force accumulates strain over its full loaded length.

options.label: δ=P(L/2)/(AE)
options.reason: There is no change in load or section at midlength.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Accumulate elastic strain along the full bar

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the elongation
gates.hint: Keep N and mm units consistent.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Stress, strain, and elongation close consistently

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: The bar is 2000 mm long, not 1000 mm.

evidence_choices.label: 0.0004×2000=0.80 mm
evidence_choices.reason: This applies strain over the full bar length.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Limit elongation to 0.50 mm
gates.constraint: Keep P, L, and E unchanged.

options.label: Increase area to at least 1600 mm²

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply axial deformation again
gates.prompt: P=60 kN, L=1500 mm, A=750 mm², E=200 GPa. What is δ?

options.label: 0.30 mm
options.reason: That effectively uses only half the member length.

gates.explanation: For a uniform elastic bar, elongation scales with PL/(AE).

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the axial-deformation calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that elastic axial elongation accumulates over the full loaded length of a uniform prismatic member.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Only half the member length was used.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The entire prismatic bar carries the axial force.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use δ=PL/(AE) over the full loaded length.

seo.meta_description: Solve FE Civil E-113: an 80 kN load on a 2 m steel bar with A=1000 mm² and E=200 GPa causes 0.80 mm elongation, not 0.40.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Civil axial deformation prismatic bar
seo.excerpt: A correct axial strain still gives the wrong elongation if it is applied over the wrong member length.
seo.direct_answer: σ=80 MPa, ε=0.0004, and δ=PL/(AE)=0.80 mm.

faqs.q: What is the elastic axial-deformation formula for a prismatic bar?
faqs.a: δ=PL/(AE) when axial force, area, and modulus are constant.
